verdict.reasoning: Shortness of breath onset and context are described: “over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath” and “while you're sitting watching TV?” / “Yeah.” This indicates acute SOB for ~1 hour at rest.
Patient describes new, non-productive cough: “I started with a cough yesterday” and when asked if she has brought anything up: “Uh, no, I haven't, no.”

Palpitations are implied: patient says, “I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart, it's really going,” and doctor clarifies, “So, you're feeling your heart more than normal?” / Patient: “Yeah.”

No chest pain but soreness with deep breath: Doctor: “And, the shortness of breath, does it cause any pain in your chest?” Patient: “Um, no.” Then, “How about when you take a very deep breath in?” Patient: “Um, I mean, yeah. My chest feels sore, but so does my C-section scar.”
C-section timing given: “I had a C-section a few weeks ago.”; Doctor: “how long ago was that? Just a few weeks?” Patient: “Yeah, four weeks.”
Codeine use and stopping: Patient: “they gave me some, uh, Codeine.”; “I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly. But, probably haven't taken it for a week.”
Patient links symptoms with stress/anxiety: “I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart, it's really going.” This supports increased stress/anxiety with symptoms.
Infant well without respiratory symptoms: Doctor: “And, how is baby doing?” Patient: “Yeah.”; Doctor: “Any coughs or colds with, uh, them?” Patient: “No, no. He's fine.”
Past surgical history: “I had a C-section a few weeks ago.” and clarified as “Yeah, four weeks.”
Postoperative codeine use: Patient: “they gave me some, uh, Codeine.”; “I've been taking that fairly, fairly regularly. But, probably haven't taken it for a week.”
Allergy with unspecified reaction: Patient: “I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.” When asked what happens, she replies, “I don't know. Sorry.” Reaction is indeed unspecified.
Family history of clots in legs: Patient: “my mum's had, uh, clots in her legs before.” This is consistent with maternal leg clots (likely DVT).
Home situation: Doctor: “And, are you with baby at the moment?” Patient: “Yes, I am.” and later, “Is anyone else with you at home?” Patient: “Uh, no. My partner's at work.”
Self-transport plan: Doctor offers ambulance vs self-transport: “Which one would you prefer?” Patient: “I will, I will go. I will, I will take myself.”

Pulse counted as 30 in 18 seconds: Doctor times pulse and asks, “How many did you count?” Patient: “Uh, I counted thirty.” The doctor responds, “your heart is running slightly fast at the moment,” which corresponds to ~100 bpm and mild tachycardia.

Doctor explicitly expresses concern for clots/PE: “Given that you've had a C-section, and you're short of breath... It might be worth you going into the hospital...” and later, “Some people can suffer with clots. And, those can either be found in the legs or your chest, so in your lungs.” The clinical inference that this presentation raises concern for VTE/PE is directly aligned with this reasoning.

The transcript does not mention postpartum anxiety, viral URI, or post-op pain as part of a formal differential diagnosis. Anxiety/stress is noted only as the patient’s reaction (“I'm getting really stressed out”), but not listed as diagnostic possibilities, and viral URI/post-op pain are not discussed as differentials.
Recent C-section as postoperative state is explicit: “I had a C-section a few weeks ago.” and clarified to four weeks, a standard postoperative state.
Medication allergy: “I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.” This is a documented allergy to ibuprofen.

Doctor advises hospital evaluation but does not specify ED workup details: no mention of vitals, ECG, D-dimer, imaging, troponin/BNP, CXR, labs, or lower limb ultrasound. These investigation details are not in the transcript.

Self-presentation and promptness: Doctor: “Or, you can take yourself to the hospital with baby.” Patient chooses self-transport: “I will, I will take myself.” Doctor adds, “go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time.”
Codeine advice: Doctor: “And, if you're taking any medications like Codeine, don't, don't take them for the time being.”

While the doctor initially offers an ambulance as an option (“I can call an ambulance. Or, you can take yourself to the hospital”), there is no explicit safety-net instruction such as ‘if symptoms worsen or you cannot travel, call an ambulance.’ That conditional safety-net phrasing is not present.

The transcript notes the allergy (“I'm allergic to Ibuprofen, though.”) but does not include any plan to document it in ED or clarify the reaction there. That future documentation/clarification step is not mentioned.
